description: Our team aims to develop Space Health Monitor, an AI-assisted software that helps astronauts monitor their physical and mental health during long-duration space missions. It tracks vital signs, sleep, stress, and activity, detects unusual health patterns, and provides timely alerts with actionable guidance. With offline access, health trend analysis, and secure data management, the system supports proactive health monitoring and safer space exploration.
summary:
AstroMind is a web-based astronaut health and cognitive wellness monitoring prototype designed to support crew members during space missions. We developed an integrated dashboard using React, TypeScript, Node.js, and Python that brings together health check-ins, cognitive assessments, telemetry monitoring, trends, and alerts. It includes interactive body mapping, reaction-time, memory and attention tests, and a health journal to track sleep, fatigue, stress, mood, and symptoms.

AstroMind addresses the challenge of monitoring astronaut wellbeing in remote space environments by combining physical health indicators, cognitive performance, and self-reported wellness in one platform. It uses personal baselines, configurable thresholds, and anomaly-monitoring outputs to highlight potential changes that may require attention. Its public demo allows evaluators to explore the application without login credentials.

This project is important because astronauts operate in demanding environments where early awareness of physical and cognitive changes can support better health monitoring and mission readiness. AstroMind demonstrates a modular approach to more accessible, context-aware astronaut wellness support while keeping model outputs informational rather than presenting them as medical diagnoses.
details:
AstroMind is a web-based astronaut health and wellness monitoring platform designed to support astronauts during space missions. It brings physical health monitoring, cognitive assessments, wellness check-ins, trends, and alerts together in one place.

The application allows astronauts to monitor important health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, body temperature, respiration, and other health-related measurements. It also includes simple cognitive games to check memory, attention, and reaction time. Through the health journal, astronauts can record their sleep, stress, fatigue, mood, and symptoms. The dashboard helps them review their progress, understand changes over time, and identify unusual patterns through alerts and anomaly scores.

We developed AstroMind using React, TypeScript, and Vite for the frontend, Node.js for the backend, and Python for telemetry processing. We used Neon PostgreSQL for storing telemetry data and browser local storage for demo records. We also included a BLE receiver workflow for collecting sensor readings and an anomaly detection workflow for identifying unusual patterns.

The main idea behind AstroMind is to look at astronaut health as a whole rather than focusing only on vital signs. Physical health, mental wellbeing, sleep, and cognitive performance are all connected. By bringing these details together, the platform can provide a better picture of an astronaut's overall wellbeing.

One of the important things we considered was the limited availability of medical support during space missions. We also focused on making the application simple to use, easy to understand, and accessible to evaluators without requiring login credentials. The interactive body map and personalized health trends make the experience more engaging and useful.

Our aim is to help astronauts and mission-support teams become more aware of possible health changes and take appropriate action when needed. AstroMind is currently a prototype, and its alerts and model outputs are intended for informational purposes rather than medical diagnosis. We hope this project can contribute to the idea of safer, smarter, and more comprehensive health monitoring for future space missions.
